readers.restyleSeam: None of the HUD scripts exports anything; each is one closure mixing logic and view. Cleanest switch: the composition root starts either the old module or a new one, never both, so the old stays byte-identical. New views can call the same remotes, bindables and shared map/card/cash modules. Notifications are the easy case: add a second controller with the same return shape and choose at SharedTopNotificationUI line 17. Onboarding should stay one owner and restyle through RacingUIComponents.
risks: The style switch cannot read Core.FeatureFlags on the client: it is server-only in ServerStorage. A replicated value must exist before ClientBase starts, and early joiners on a fresh server may get the default.
Onboarding resolves targets by name, text and attribute. A new view that renames or re-nests them loses its tutorial silently (page never begins, or is abandoned after 3 s).
Style sheet removes the customise hub screen: tutorial page CustomisationHome (steps J1-J3) loses its three target cards. The page id is saved, server allow-listed state.
Any new GuiButton named Car, Race or Garage is disabled by applyLocks for players who have not seen that shortcut page, and may be picked as the highlight target.

Old and new presentations must never run together: both would call RouteGuide.Update per frame, write the mobile menu attributes and MobileDriveInputState, and destroy each other's same-named ScreenGui.
Changing the typeface breaks text measurement in onboarding bubbles and notifications, which measure with Enum.Font.Michroma by literal.
FullMapUI needs a ScreenGui named MobileFreeRoamHud_Phase1 with a descendant Minimap to allow keyboard/controller map open; a new HUD must keep both names.
The free-roam telemetry cluster doubles as the in-race gauge, so the free-roam HUD and in-race HUD build steps share one owner per platform.

Mobile HUD and touch controls lay out from full Camera.ViewportSize with constant margins inside a device-safe-inset ScreenGui; no real safe-area maths (HUD 347-365, controls 177-192). Not verified in Play.
Touch pedals are a fixed 125 px and the boost plate 44/52 px while arrows and thumbstick scale with height (MobileDriveControlsClient 185-191); HUD has one hard breakpoint at vp.Y<500.
OnboardingClient polls every 0.2 s for the whole session with repeated full PlayerGui walks (666-671, 757) and a full workspace walk inside owned garages (649).
Onboarding callouts have no keyboard or gamepad advance path, and locked shortcut buttons show no locked state (669).
Top notifications measure regular Michroma but draw bold (foundation 480 vs 550), have no severity or de-duplication, and sit top-centre where the in-race timer is planned.
readers.mobileAndInput: Mobile HUD and touch controls are touch-only (Activated, InputBegan/Ended, gyroscope); no gamepad selection or ContextActionService in any of the five scripts. Platform choice is made once at start by two non-complementary gates. Mobile detection differs across the place (TouchEnabled; touch without keyboard; short side 650/700). Three safe-area methods coexist; only Foundation.Confirmation computes real device insets. StarterGui.ScreenOrientation is LandscapeSensor. Three settings rows on mobile (graphics, UI scale, speed unit) do nothing.

Not shared: the mobile HUD's own panel/label/button, segmented control, dropdown and modal shell; touch-control primitives; minimap pan/rotate/zoom maths (copied in both HUDs); any safe-area or form-factor helper. Restyling shared components alone will not reach the mobile HUD or touch controls.

readers.restyleSeam: Every script is one closure exporting only start(); no stop, no API. Logic and view cannot be separated without editing them. Cleanest switch: a style-keyed path override in ClientBase's resolver (L105-109) so exactly one module per surface starts, leaving old scripts byte-identical. Swap HUD, results, countdown, queue banner and route guide; keep RaceTransitionClient and RaceLifecyclePresentationClient single and unchanged. New modules listen to the same RaceEvent and call the same remote actions. No other script references these ScreenGui names.
readers.sharedComponents: All text and panels go through RacingUIComponents (Panel = Frame + UICorner + two UIStrokes; Button = 7 instances with mouse-only hover; Michroma from Config.UI.Racing.Typography). The in-race exit confirmation copies ConfirmationLayout numbers instead of using Foundation.Confirmation. Four separate canvas-scaling implementations exist in this group. Recommend lifting the HUD's safe-area canvas (L83-116) into the foundation, with a touch-aware minimum, for HUD, countdown, queue banner and WRONG WAY, plus pooled rows for order and results tables.
readers.mobileAndInput: Touch: HUD uses InRace.Mobile sizes, hides the race map, stacks RESET/EXIT at a fixed X of 700. The same uniform scale applies, so on an 844x390 phone 48-unit buttons render about 17 px tall and row text about 5 px (by source, not captured). Results use the desktop shell at about 0.43 scale. Input is mouse/touch only: no keyboard shortcuts, no GuiService selection, no ContextActionService; results buttons use MouseButton1Click, so a controller cannot press them.
defects: In-race HUD reappears after finishing or exiting a multiplayer race: RaceSessionPresentationClient L313 calls show() on any RacePositionUpdate with no active session, and the server broadcasts positions to finished and exited players (MatchmakingServer L646-661, L704-706). By source; needs a two-client test.

Phone sizes: HUD canvas scale is not touch-aware (L98-107), giving roughly 17 px tall RESET/EXIT buttons and 5 px row text on 844x390; queue LEAVE about 20 px tall; results at about 0.43 scale. Breaks the 48 px touch target rule. By source.

Results do not grow above 1080p: RacingUIComponents.AttachResponsiveScale clamps at ScaleMax 1.15, so the 1200x720 shell covers about 40% of the width at 3440x1440 and 36% at 4K. Three different scaling paths in one screen.
Time-trial results have no buttons until GetTimeTrialLeaderboard returns: renderTimeTrial yields at L140 and builds the footer at L143. A slow or hung call strands the player on the results screen.

Wholesale rebuilds: HUD board destroyed and recreated on every race event (L273, L286); race results fully rebuilt on every RacePositionUpdate while open (L216), twice at the finish. Time-trial lap board grows without bound in infinite-lap runs and clips the newest laps.

Exit confirmation is hand-built (RaceSessionPresentationClient L175-182) rather than the shared Foundation.Confirmation: no Escape or gamepad B cancel, no focus, different z-order; the destructive YES is styled as the primary action. Results buttons use MouseButton1Click with no busy guard.

WRONG WAY prompt is fixed pixels (280x38 at y=178) in an unscaled ScreenGui under the HUD, so the scaled centre card covers it at 4K; the checkpoint pill is offset-sized and never scales. Route guide is not cleared on RaceExitedToStart or RaceDNF (L427).

Per-frame waste: time-trial timer text rewritten every frame in a proportional face (L317, digits jitter); RaceRouteGuideClient Heartbeat does config-folder lookups every frame for the whole session including free roam; RaceTransitionClient handles every race payload twice (L385-391).
risks: The style flag is not client-readable: FeatureFlags lives in ServerStorage.Modules.Core and reads ConfigService. ClientBase needs a replicated value that is present before it resolves entries, with a safe default to the old style.

RaceLifecyclePresentationClient destroys any ScreenGui named RaceHud, RaceHud_Phase3, RaceCheckpointBadge_Phase5D, RaceQueue_Phase8, RaceSessionControls_Phase8C/8D, RaceResults_Phase4, TimeTrialResultCoach, RaceEntry, RaceEntryProbe or TimeTrialPersonalBestBoard. New surfaces must avoid these names.
A replacement countdown must set Runtime.Racing attribute CountdownPresentationReady, or RaceTransitionClient waits 7.5 s and acknowledges every race start as degraded.

RaceQueueClient is the JoinQueue owner. Running old and new together, or adding a second StartRaceQueueRequest listener, sends JoinQueue twice. Same single-owner rule for RESET/EXIT, results actions and the RaceSession, RaceQueue and RaceResults presentation owner keys.

Results hero number for driver XP has no source: neither RaceFinished nor TimeTrialFinished carries XP. It arrives later as player attributes Rank and XpIntoRank. Showing it from the payload means a server payload change, which the sheet excludes.

Timer delta chip: per-checkpoint delta against the saved personal best needs PB splits the server does not send. Only lap-end delta against BestSeconds or a client-kept session-best lap is possible without a server change.

Race results sit on a full black fade (RaceTransitionClient holds fadeOut on RaceFinished and the server destroys the race car 0.45 s later); time-trial results sit over the dimmed scene. A results design that assumes scenery behind it will differ by mode.

RaceTransitionClient must not be forked, yet its status label hard-codes Michroma and a mint-white colour. Either accept it under the new style or declare a small token-read exception. The custom Start banner needs ProximityPrompt Style=Custom, which a server script sets today.
unknowns: Rendered sizes at 1280x720, 3440x1440 and on phones are computed from source; no Play session or device capture was allowed.
The HUD-reappears and guide-persists findings come from reading client and server together and need a two-client Play test.
RaceSessionAssetsClient, RaceParticipantVisibilityClient and ReplicatedFirst.Loading.LoadingTransitionRuntime (the real race loading screen) were outside this group and not read.
Whether GetTimeTrialLeaderboard can be slow enough to strand players depends on GlobalLeaderboardServer, which was not read.

Whether the medal table, global top 20, lap list and finishing order stay on the restyled results screen: the mockup shows only two hero numbers and one strip, but the data and current screen include them.
The sheet makes Continue the main results button; today the race-again button is the highlighted one. Needs Oscar's decision.
Whether the RaceEvent copy of RaceStaged omits ParticipantCount was read only to MatchmakingServer L975.

readers.restyleSeam: FullMapUI has no internal seam: logic and view share one closure. Leave it untouched; add a new full-map module with the same API (Open/Close/Toggle/IsOpen/start) and have ClientBase start exactly one. MapMarkers, MapMath, MapTileSet and RouteGuide state stay shared. MapIconLayer, RouteGuide's renderer and MapMath need small additive, default-off options (circle shape, tint, chip placement, route getter). Player markers take a second config folder.
readers.sharedComponents: Full map uses RacingUIComponents (Panel, Label, Button, Corner, Stroke, Colour) with Racing.Colours. Both minimaps and the full map share MapTileSet, MapIconLayer, RouteGuide.newMapRenderer and FreeRoamMapPlayerMarkers. Not shared: map transform maths (five copies), speedZoomFactor (two copies), asset-id normaliser (five copies), the route chip (fixed style in code), legend rows (hand-built).
readers.mobileAndInput: isMobile fixed at start (touch and no keyboard). Phone: 44 px minimum targets, narrower legend auto-closed below 760 px wide, larger icons and tap radius, pinch zoom. Keyboard: M, Esc, E/Q, C, F, Backspace, WASD. Gamepad through ContextActionService only (Select, A, B, X, Y, LB/RB, left stick, crosshair); no GuiService selection, legend not scrollable by controller. Mobile minimap is top-right; desktop bottom-left.
defects: FullMapUI 374-430: text has no floor; on phones s=0.55 gives 6 to 8 px hint, legend, district and close text.
FullMapUI 112, 377-394: no safe-area or top-bar handling; header buttons sit 8 to 40 px from the screen edge under the Roblox top bar and notches.
FullMapUI 128-129 with RouteGuide 202, 334: rotated route segments are probably not clipped by the plain MapView frame and can draw over header and margins (not verified in Play).
FullMapUI 374, 143, 819: scale capped at 1.12 so chrome shrinks on 1440p and 4K; map icons (48 px) and route width never follow the scale.
RouteGuide 216-247, 382-385: chip (10 px text) and pip never scale; chip is inside the clip; edge-pip clamp is square.
MapIconLayer 114, 305-307: icons cannot be tinted; inside test and edge clamp are rectangular, so a circular clip cuts rim icons.
FullMapUI 443-444, 491, 523: legend destroyed and rebuilt on every resize and toggle; player markers and their connections rebuilt on every open.
Per-frame config re-reads and allocation: FullMapUI 773-806, RouteGuide 304-394, Desktop HUD 1147-1224 (about 25 FindFirstChild reads per frame for the minimap).
risks: Old and new full map must never both start: both write FullMapOpen, bind M, ButtonSelect and the same action and render-step names, own the Waypoint source, and a same-named gui is destroyed at start.
FullMapUI opens from M/Back only if ScreenGuis DesktopFreeRoamHud or MobileFreeRoamHud_Phase1 contain a visible child named Minimap; a renamed new HUD silently breaks the old map's toggle.
HUD owners reach the map by module name FullMapUI; a new HUD must call the new module or the open fails with MAP NOT AVAILABLE.
RouteGuide and MapMarkers are singletons shared by both styles; any non-additive change to them alters the backup UI. Config.UI.RouteGuide ChipEnabled is global, not per style.
No minimap runs during a race today (cluster hidden, map step paused, full map blocked). The sheet's in-race minimap is new behaviour and new frame cost, not a restyle.
Round minimap relies on CanvasGroup clipping; CanvasGroup textures may render softer on low-memory phones and the clip edge needs the ring drawn over it.
A long route holds an estimated 400 to 1,200 GUI instances per renderer with no spatial culling; a larger round minimap with speed zoom re-lays them out inside a CanvasGroup each frame.
Style-sheet conflicts needing a decision: full-map key-hint strip, untinted full-colour map icons, phone minimap position (top-right today), pink activity route colour.
unknowns: Whether route segments visibly spill outside the full map view when zoomed in (needs Play).
Native pixel size of the 16 map tiles and whether seams show on the 4x supersampled minimap canvas.
Real route point counts (estimated 100 to 300 from RoadRouting.Smooth at 8 samples per corner).
CanvasGroup sharpness and cost on a low-end phone at 307 px.
Instance count added per button by ResponsiveUIFoundation.ApplyBevel (not read in this group).
Whether the HUD scale applies to the mobile minimap icons as intended (raw pixels there, scaled on desktop).

Owners: one owner per state, geometry, visibility, preview, attachment and persistence concern. Never add an owner to overpower an existing one; retire, narrow or replace instead (AGENTS.md, docs/14). The restyle may change what existing owners draw, not who draws.

findings.conclusion: Staff guidance is fixed-offset content in anchored clusters; Roblox units are device-independent, so phones draw them at 2-3x. Scale-based sizing is discouraged. A per-cluster UIScale keeps text crisp but gives fractional sizes. The sheet's anchored-cluster direction is right; one full-screen scaled canvas is not.

At 720p and 1440p the scale is 0.667 and 1.333, so a 2 px hairline becomes 1.33 or 2.67 px. How the engine snaps that is undocumented; community reports show one-pixel inconsistencies. Integer-rounded thickness is the safe rule, but it needs a capture test before the component library is fixed.

Studio probe: TextSize 136 and 200 both read back 100, UITextSizeConstraint.MaxTextSize also clamps to 100, and text measurement clamps at 100. The sheet's SpeedNumber (136) and HeroNumber (200) need a UIScale on the label or digit sprites. Crispness above 100 under UIScale is unconfirmed.

Animating UIScale on a subtree containing text causes flicker; staff ticketed it in October 2024 and no fix is shown. Tweening text size is called potentially game-breaking. Pressed 96% and selected 110% should snap, or scale a layer that holds no text.

Flex (UIFlexItem, HorizontalFlex) is released and unused in the game; it suits button rows, tab rows and label-bar-value stat rows at a slight documented cost. AutomaticSize costs about one text measurement; TextScaled about ten. Layout cost scales with elements resized or reparented per ScreenGui.

AutomaticCanvasSize is wrong under an ancestor UIScale when children use Scale sizes (staff backlog, still reported January 2026); fixed-offset tiles avoid it. ScrollingFrames always clip and accept neither UICorner nor UIGradient, so the enlarged selected tile and its glow need padding or an overlay.

Width probe: Titillium Web ExtraBold measures identical to Bold in both styles, and Heavy Italic identical to Bold Italic. The sheet's ExtraBold Italic roles would silently render as Bold Italic. Bold Italic and SemiBold Italic exist. Italic widths differ by only 1-2 px, so confirm by eye.

Titillium Web digits are already uniform: every digit measures 37.33 px at size 100 in Bold Italic and SemiBold Italic. Roboto Condensed is also uniform; Oswald is not. Changing numbers will not jitter in a fixed-size, edge-aligned label. OpenType tnum is not needed and not officially confirmed.

GuiService.PreferredTextSize changes text in experience UI: TextScaled labels are exempt, UITextSizeConstraint caps it, AutomaticSize elements grow, and text measurement honours it. Dense fixed panels can overflow for players on Large to Largest unless capped or tested.

Styling is fully released (2026-01-20; StyleQuery 2026-05-11; Transitions 2026-07-27). It is not a sound theme switch here: rules do not apply to properties code has set away from defaults, the old UI is not style-driven, one sheet per ScreenGui, and there is no gamepad-focus state.

A ScreenGui's appearance is cached until any descendant or property changes; one change recomputes the whole ScreenGui. Staff advise separating static from dynamic UI and avoiding frequent writes to non-visual descendants. Gauge, minimap and timer should not share a ScreenGui with static chrome.

Published guidance: under 300 UIStrokes on screen for low-end devices, at most 100 UIShadows, at most 1000 gradients (six or fewer colour stops; animate offset or rotation, not colour). UIGradient and UICorner on text labels are flagged as costly. The square, stroke-free style sits well inside these.

CanvasGroup renders to a texture sized to its AbsoluteSize, only under ZIndexBehavior.Sibling. Texture quality is capped by QualityLevel; low settings may downscale and throttle it, and over the memory cap it renders blank. Direct-child modifiers such as UIShadow ignore GroupTransparency. Use it only where clipping or a group fade is unavoidable.

UIShadow was announced fully released on 2026-06-23. It supports coloured glow, does not affect layout, and is stated to be faster than 9-sliced images. It does not work on Path2D and can look jagged on large corner radii. It can replace the planned glow uploads for tiles and buttons.

Studio v742 exposes UIShadow.Mode = Text, Inset, ShowBehindParent and a UIBlur class. Only the ApplyShadowMode enum is documented; the class page still says text is unsupported and UIBlur has no docs. Live-client support is unconfirmed, so title shadows still need a scrim or duplicate label.

Transparent pixels become black on upload, so soft images need alpha bleeding. Author at about twice the displayed offset size because phones draw at 2-3x. Sprite sheets load faster for many small icons. The stored maximum resolution for UI images is unconfirmed.

Path2D has been released since 2024-06-17 and can draw arcs as Bezier segments and a static route outline (100 control points maximum, thickness up to 100 px, gradient supported). It has no Transparency, no shadow and no native clipping. A filling speed arc needs per-frame control-point updates of unknown cost and edge quality.

The minimap is already a CanvasGroup with rotated tiles, markers and route. ClipsDescendants cannot clip to rounded corners, and a mask image cannot hide content over a live scene, so the round map is the same CanvasGroup with UICorner at 0.5 scale. Roughly 0.4 MB at 1x and 3.4 MB at 3x.

Engine navigation offers GuiService:Select, SelectionGroup with Stop or Escape per direction, SelectionOrder, SelectionChanged and SelectionImageObject. The game uses almost none of it: SelectedObject appears only in the confirmation dialog. White-fill focus needs the default adornment replaced by an invisible object and the fill driven from selection events.

Official pattern: backgrounds in a ScreenGui with ScreenInsets None, interactive content in a safe-inset ScreenGui; avoid FullscreenExtension for new work. GuiService:GetInsetArea and TopbarInset give exact rectangles. The foundation and race HUD already clamp with GetInsetArea, so the restyle should reuse that owner.

Write a property only when the shown value changes, since every write invalidates the ScreenGui cache. Keep pooled tiles parented and rebind them; adding, removing or reparenting rebuilds the Z-order list. TweenService runs natively; the advice is fewer tweened objects. No official total-instance budget exists.

Released and usable: UIStroke inner/centre position, scaled size and multiple strokes (2025-12-04), ViewportDisplaySize (2025-10-21), PreferredInput, UIShadow and per-corner UICorner (2026-06-23). Radial and conical UIGradient were Studio Beta on 2026-09-02 and not publishable then, so they work in Studio Play but may not in a live client.

recommendations: Run a short capture spike before fixing the component library: one Panel, one tile rail and one button row at 1280x720, 1920x1080, 2560x1440, 3440x1440 and a phone emulator. Compare a per-cluster UIScale against integer-rounded metrics (px(n) = round(n * scale)) for hairline evenness, and check TextSize 100 with UIScale 1.36 and 2.0 for crispness.

Keep the sheet's anchored-cluster layout with fixed-offset content. Put every metric behind one Style function so hairline thickness is max(1, round(2 * scale)) whichever scaling route the spike picks. Do not use TextScaled on dense panels.

Change the sheet's type table: no role above 100 as a TextSize. Build SpeedNumber and HeroNumber as a label at 100 or less with its own UIScale (or digit sprites if the spike shows blur), and replace 'ExtraBold Italic' with Bold Italic unless a font with that face is chosen.
Keep changing numbers in fixed-size, right- or left-aligned labels in Titillium Web and update Text only when the displayed string changes. No per-digit labels are needed.

Do not use StyleSheets for the switch. Use a Luau Style token module reading Config.UI.Style, shared component constructors, and the Core.FeatureFlags flag choosing the old or new builder path, as the sheet proposes.

Build one Glow component with two backends: UIShadow (coloured, no upload) for the selected tile and main button, and a 9-slice image fallback. Confirm UIShadow in a published test build on a real client before dropping the image uploads. Keep gauge-arc and minimap-ring glow baked into their images.

Draw the minimap ring and rank ring with a circular Frame, an Inner or Center UIStroke and a UIGradient child on the stroke, so no ring image is needed. Keep the round minimap as the existing CanvasGroup with UICorner 0.5 scale, and replace the four straight edge fades with one vignette image.

Keep the speed gauge image-based (existing segment images or two-half rotation) behind a small GaugeArc interface, so it can move to a conical gradient once that reaches live clients. Use Path2D only for static route outlines if the existing RouteGuide renderer cannot be restyled.

Split each HUD into a static ScreenGui (status cluster, action bar, panels) and a dynamic one (gauge, minimap, timer, live order). Disable ScreenGuis that are not showing. Avoid per-frame attribute or value writes on instances under a ScreenGui.

For the tile rail: fixed-offset layout cells, an inner visual frame that takes the selected scale and glow, UIPadding large enough for the growth and glow, ScrollBarThickness 0, and CanvasSize set from AbsoluteContentSize if AutomaticCanvasSize misbehaves under UIScale. Keep tiles parented and rebind them instead of destroying and recreating.
Use flex for button rows, tab rows, the status strip and label-bar-value stat rows, replacing copied coordinates.
Snap the pressed and selected scale changes, or apply them to a background layer with no text. Reserve UIScale tweens for text-free elements.

Add gamepad focus to the shared Button and Tile: an invisible SelectionImageObject, white fill driven by SelectionGained and SelectionLost, SelectionGroup on rails and modals, GuiService:Select on open, and re-select when a selected tile is removed. Apply this only on the new-style path so the old UI keeps its default adornment.

Use GuiService.ViewportDisplaySize and UserInputService.PreferredInput for phone, desktop and controller decisions. Keep safe-area clamping in ResponsiveUIFoundation's existing GetInsetArea path; put full-bleed tints in a ScreenInsets None layer and interactive content inside the clamped area.
Add a verification row for the player Text Size setting at Largest, and cap labels that cannot grow (speed number, tile names, chips) with a UITextSizeConstraint.

Pack icons into one white-on-transparent sprite sheet authored at 2-3x with alpha bleeding and tint with ImageColor3. Keep full-screen translucent layers to two at most on phones, and treat whole-screen blur as optional on Small displays.
cautions: Studio Play is not proof for 2026 engine features. Radial and conical gradients, UIShadow Text mode, Inset, ShowBehindParent and UIBlur all exist in Studio 0.742 but have beta, partial or no release documentation. Verify each in a published build on a real client before depending on it.
UIShadow's release is stated in the announcement (2026-06-23), but one community post on 2026-07-06 still called it beta. Treat it as medium confidence until seen on a live client.

UIShadow.ShowBehindParent defaults to true in v742, so a pink glow may tint a 0.86-opacity slate panel from behind. The selected tile (white) and main button (gradient) are opaque, so they are unaffected.
The font-weight finding rests on text-width comparison. Italic widths differ by only 1-2 px between weights, so confirm the available italic faces by eye before locking the type table.

CanvasGroup needs ZIndexBehavior.Sibling. Two owners use Global (including SharedInRaceHUD), so a round CanvasGroup minimap would not clip there. On low graphics settings CanvasGroups may be downscaled, throttled or blank.
A UIShadow that is a direct child of a CanvasGroup does not fade with GroupTransparency; wrap content in an inner Frame.

I could not confirm how fractional rectangles are rasterised under UIScale, whether 9-slice corners or Path2D thickness follow UIScale, Path2D edge quality and per-frame cost, the maximum stored UI image resolution, or ScrollingFrame auto-scroll to the gamepad selection.
StarterGui.ClipsDescendantsSupportsRotation is mentioned in the docs and listed on StarterGui in v742 but was not readable from script. Do not plan on it replacing the minimap CanvasGroup.

The Studio probes created unparented temporary instances (TextLabel, UIShadow, UIBlur, Path2D, GetTextBoundsParams, UITextSizeConstraint) and destroyed them. Nothing was parented, no script was edited, Play was not started and no gameplay module was required.
Community performance claims (ScreenGui batching, CanvasGroup 'huge memory hit') conflict with each other and are not staff statements. The findings rely on docs and staff posts instead.

findings.topic: Barlow Condensed availability and custom font upload
findings.conclusion: Barlow Condensed is not in Roblox. The Creator Store lists 91 font families today, all published by Roblox; a search for "condensed" returns none. Custom fonts cannot be uploaded: the official docs say "You cannot import fonts". Six families were added in July and August 2026, so the catalogue is still growing.

Creator Store fonts work in experiences via Font.new("rbxassetid://<id>", weight, style) or Font.fromId(id, weight, style). Barlow (12187372847) and Kanit (12187373592) each have 18 faces with italics from 100 to 900. Both measured correctly in v3 with no install step. A bad id raises a clear error.

In the store: Barlow, Kanit, Fira Sans, Prompt (all with italics); Teko, Rajdhani, Antonio, Goldman (no italic). Not in the store: Saira Condensed, Big Shoulders, Fjalla One, League Gothic, Bebas Neue, Anton, Chakra Petch, Exo 2. No condensed family with an italic exists anywhere in Roblox.
findings.source: Creator Store search API listing (91 families) and family JSON files

findings.topic: Shipped families with a real italic
findings.conclusion: 43 family files ship. Real italics: Titillium Web (to weight 700 only), Roboto Condensed (300, 400, 700), Source Sans Pro (to 900), Montserrat, Roboto, Nunito, Arimo, Ubuntu, Josefin Sans, Roboto Mono, Merriweather, Fondamento. Oswald, Sarpanch, Jura, Builder Sans and Michroma have none.

findings.topic: Style sheet sizes are not Roblox TextSize
findings.conclusion: Roblox TextSize is the font's line height (model matches Studio within 2%). The sheet's sizes are CSS em sizes, confirmed by measuring the mockups. Equal cap height needs TextSize = sheet size x 1.20 for Barlow, 1.15 for Roboto Condensed, 1.57 for Titillium Web. Copied unchanged, text is 13 to 36% too small.
findings.source: Shipped TTF metrics read from disk, capsize metrics 4.3.0, GetTextBoundsAsync, assets/ui/mockups/pulse_restyle/04-customise-parts.jpg

findings.conclusion: Confirmed in Studio: TextLabel.TextSize set to 200 reads back 100, UITextSizeConstraint.MaxTextSize caps at 100, and text bounds stop growing at 100. HeroNumber 200 and SpeedNumber 136 are impossible as text sizes in any font. With Titillium Web, ScreenTitle 80 needs 125.

findings.topic: Width against the mockup face at equal cap height
findings.conclusion: Versus Barlow Condensed ExtraBold Italic: Roboto Condensed Bold Italic about +12%, Titillium Web Bold Italic +19%, Barlow ExtraBold Italic +22%, Kanit +42%, Michroma +92%. Upright Oswald Bold matches the mockup width; Antonio Bold is 21% narrower. The sheet's "10 to 15% wider" understates Titillium.
findings.source: GetTextBoundsAsync at Size 100 on four strings, divided by cap height; mockup ink measured from the JPEG (about 5% error)

findings.topic: Titillium Web as the sheet's recommended face
findings.conclusion: Titillium Web has no italic above Bold, so the sheet's ExtraBold Italic roles would render as Bold Italic. Its caps are only 44.7% of TextSize, the lowest of the candidates except Kanit, so it hits the 100 cap soonest. The sheet's claim that Roboto Condensed is 20% wider holds only at equal TextSize.
findings.source: TitilliumWeb.json faces; measured ExtraBold and Heavy Italic widths equal Bold Italic (279)

findings.conclusion: Titillium Web, Roboto Condensed and Source Sans Pro have fixed-width digits. Barlow, Kanit, Oswald, Antonio and Teko do not: in Barlow ten 1s measure 119 px and ten 0s 187 px. TextLabel.OpenTypeFeatures exists and accepted "tnum", but its effect could not be measured without parenting a label.
findings.source: GetTextBoundsAsync on "1111111111" and "0000000000" at Bold Italic, Size 40

findings.conclusion: Every italic face is a cloud asset fetched at run time, including Titillium Web Bold Italic and Roboto Condensed Bold Italic; only a few upright faces are on disk. A shipped family has no loading advantage for italics. ContentProvider:PreloadAsync on a text object waits for its fonts; LoadingScreenView already preloads other assets.
findings.source: Family JSON assetId fields (rbxasset vs rbxassetid); https://devforum.roblox.com/t/new-font-ui-live/1967004

findings.conclusion: Five config values name Michroma: three FontFamily URIs plus DesktopFreeRoamHud.Typography.PrimaryFont and BodyFont by name. DesktopFreeRoamHudUI line 170 resolves through Enum.Font, which cannot express Bold Italic or a store family. Scripts hold 24 Michroma literals in 16 scripts and 19 Enum.Font uses in 14.
findings.source: Config.UI scan and script pattern counts in v3; script_grep PrimaryFont / FontFamily

findings.conclusion: Config.UI holds 130 asset references; scripts hold no UI image ids. Most icons are pure white 256 px glyphs tintable in code. Exceptions with baked colour: BoostIcon (blue), ModuleLockIcon (grey with halo), MapPlayerIcon (pink), four mobile control images (teal), 14 map icons, MedalAtlas. Full list with ids is in the notes.
findings.source: Read-only Config.UI scan and in-memory EditableImage reads in v3

findings.topic: Style sheet icons: have or missing
findings.conclusion: Have: car, garage, race flag, tools, settings, exit door, back arrow, drive wheel, wrench, paint, save, cart. Outline-only in the racing atlas: route, laps, checkpoints, players, trophy, loop, pin. Missing: teleport pin, set route, tick, gamepad, upgrade arrow, coin. Redraw in white: lock, boost. All glow, ring, gauge and title-mark images are new.
findings.source: Config.UI scan; assets/ui/icons/racing/racing-ui-icon-atlas.png; coarse alpha previews of live images

findings.conclusion: Icon padding varies: ink fills 75% of the canvas on BackIcon and 97 to 100% on Exit, Paint, Settings and Drive, so icons look different sizes in one frame. The racing atlas is thin outline art beside solid glyphs. Light grey slot diagrams will nearly vanish on the white selected tile.
findings.source: Ink-box measurements from live images; compose_diagrams.py GREY = (226, 228, 234)

findings.conclusion: Images were drawn offline with Python: Pillow or a stdlib PNG codec for icons (scripts/map_art), numpy for glow and ring textures (scripts/hover_feel/vfx_textures), Blender plus Pillow for slot diagrams (scripts/exotic_category/mesh). Pillow 12.3.0 is installed. Existing uploads can be read back through EditableImage in Edit (scripts/map_art/export_icons.lua).

Two proven routes: Studio MCP upload_image fed by a local server on 127.0.0.1:8767, and Open Cloud scripts/exotic_category/mesh/upload_image.py using the ROBLOX_ASSETS_KEY variable. Neither is recorded as needing manual steps, but project rules require Oscar's explicit approval per asset. Uploads cannot be updated; each revision is a new id and is moderated.

recommendations: Choose the typeface from a three-way Studio capture before locking the sheet: Barlow ExtraBold Italic (rbxassetid://12187372847), Roboto Condensed Bold Italic and Titillium Web Bold Italic on the Customise screen at 1280x720, 1920x1080 and 3440x1440, in a throwaway Play-only ScreenGui. My pick is Barlow: it is the mockup's own design and has the 800 and 900 italics.

Store the font as tokens in Config.UI.Style.Typography: FontFamily (content URI), DisplayWeight, LabelWeight, Style, CapHeightRatio and BaselineShift. Shared label builders size by cap height and centre caps optically, and a later swap to Barlow Condensed is one edit.
Rewrite the sheet's size table as cap heights (sheet size x 0.70) and derive TextSize from CapHeightRatio. Do not copy the CSS numbers into TextSize.

Draw speed, hero cash and XP, and race position from a digit sprite sheet (0 to 9 and , . : $ % + -) tinted with ImageColor3. It avoids the 100 cap, gives fixed-width digits and stays sharp at 4K, and can use the real Barlow Condensed ExtraBold Italic under its Open Font License. Needs Oscar's approval to fetch the font file and upload.
If Barlow is chosen, give every other changing number (cash chip, timer, stat values) fixed-width digit cells, or prove OpenTypeFeatures = "tnum" works in the bake-off capture.
Preload the chosen font faces in ReplicatedFirst.Loading.LoadingScreenView with ContentProvider:PreloadAsync, since all italic faces are cloud assets.
Replace the Enum.Font resolver in DesktopFreeRoamHudUI (line 170) with Font.new(family, weight, style) and route the 19 Enum.Font literals through the shared label builder.

Build one new icon sheet (1024 px, 128 px cells with gutters, pure white, one ink box for every glyph). Export the existing white glyphs with the EditableImage route and re-centre them; draw the missing and outline-only ones solid: pin, set route, tick, loop, gamepad, upgrade arrow, coin, lock, boost, trophy, route, laps, checkpoints, players.
Put new ids in Config.UI.Style.Icons and Style.Glow and leave every existing asset folder untouched, so switching back to the old UI needs no asset work.

Upload once, after Oscar approves a contact sheet: icon sheet, two or three glow 9-slices, ring glow, gauge arcs, title mark, digit sheet and four restyled mobile control images (about ten files). Record ids in a new scripts/ui_restyle/uploaded_assets.json.
Add right padding of about 0.2 x cap height to italic labels in the shared builder so the last slanted letter is not clipped in tight or auto-sized labels.

Give selected (white) tiles a dark tint on slot-diagram images or keep a dark image well, and decide whether Exotic dealership tiles get car images (open issue EXO-03) before building the dealership rail.
cautions: No candidate font was rendered or viewed. All font results are width and metric measurements; the look, weight and sharpness still need a Studio capture.

Under a UIScale above 1, text beyond an effective size of 100 is reported by developers to look soft. This was not verified in Studio. Fonts with small caps for their line height (Titillium Web, Kanit) would suffer most.
Whether Roblox fakes a slant for families without an italic was not established. Assume it does not; do not plan on italic Oswald or Antonio.
Width comparisons against the mockup carry about 5% error (ink measured from a JPEG against advance widths).
Image tint only darkens. The blue boost icon, grey lock, pink map arrow, teal mobile controls and coloured map icons cannot be recoloured in code to white, cyan or yellow.
Descriptions of the less obvious glyphs (Buy, Owned, Customise, Decorations) come from a coarse alpha preview, not a viewed image. Sizes, ids and colour figures are exact.
RaceBrowserClient.ICON_CELLS holds optical offsets hand-tuned beside Michroma; they will be wrong beside a new font.
Uploaded images cannot be edited or removed by the tools here. Each revision adds an asset to Oscar's inventory, and each is moderated before other players see it.
Creator Store fonts depend on Roblox keeping the asset available. Keep the sheet's fall-back-and-warn-once rule for a family that fails to load.
The TextSize-is-line-height model was checked against shipped font files; metrics for store families (Barlow, Kanit, Antonio) come from the published capsize data, not from Roblox's own copies.

Beyond the notes file I wrote four small helper scripts and one saved API response under ui_restyle_audit/tools in the scratchpad. Nothing in the repo or the Studio place was changed, no font file was downloaded, and no upload tool was called.

uncoveredGroups.why: Street Life views draw strip text, offer and stake cards, countdowns, beacons and toasts through ActivityClient.Context, and create two native prompts (RIDE, job). A restyled ctx.UI must keep that contract. They pass Telemetry, HighSpeed and ElectricBlue as meaning, which the five new colour roles do not cover.

Server scripts create or toggle the race-start, vehicle Enter, Drive Out, Manage Garage and exit prompts, all Style Default. The sheet's Start banner with a key cap needs Style Custom set here and on templates. That is a server edit the sheet's client-only contract excludes; TimeTrialServer also writes personal bests.

These react to UI rather than draw it. PresentationAudioClient adds hover and click sounds to every GuiButton and reads four UIAudio attributes. Two scripts look up PlayerGui.DriveHUD and toggle Roblox TouchGui. RaceParticipantVisibilityClient disables any BillboardGui or name tag on other racers. DrivingCameraClient's speed-line overlay was only partly read.

Studio-only surfaces: a telemetry panel at DisplayOrder 2000 in Enum.Font.Code, a Roblox core notification for test cash, and trailer mode, the only SetCoreGuiEnabled caller, which disables every ScreenGui. Confirm they are excluded from the restyle and that trailer mode still hides the new ScreenGuis.

otherSurfaces: Player list: leaderstats (Cash) exists and nothing disables the PlayerList CoreGui, so Roblox's leaderboard draws top-right, where the sheet puts the status cluster and action bar. Decide: disable it, or move the cluster.

Chat: the TextChatService window is enabled, top-left, BuilderSans 18 on grey. It overlaps the sheet's screen title, event card and in-race position. Decide its position and whether ChatWindowConfiguration and ChatInputBarConfiguration take the new font and slate colour, or chat hides in menus and races.
Bubble chat and voice: white bubbles in BuilderSans 20, default voice on. Decide whether BubbleChatConfiguration is restyled to slate and white or left as the Roblox default.

Top bar: every ScreenGui sets IgnoreGuiInset and no script reads GuiService.TopbarInset. The sheet's 58 px HUD margin and top-left titles can sit under Roblox's menu and chat buttons. Decide one inset rule for all screens.

Proximity prompts: about ten prompt families (race start, vehicle Enter, RIDE, job, dealership, customisation, drive-in, garage entry, Drive Out, Manage, Exit) use the default Roblox style. No PromptShown handler exists. Decide whether one custom prompt renderer is in scope.

Name tags and health: default Roblox name and health bars show above characters within 100 studs; no custom name tag exists. Decide whether to hide health, keep default names, or add a styled name tag (a new world component that race visibility would toggle).

Gamepad selection box: SelectionImageObject is never set, so Roblox's default selection outline will draw on top of the sheet's white-fill focus state. Decide on a custom selection image or a transparent one.

On-foot touch controls: Roblox's thumbstick and jump button (TouchGui) occupy the bottom corners on phones, and two scripts toggle TouchGui.Enabled. The sheet's bottom-left minimap and bottom-right gauge compete with them when the player is on foot.

Purchase prompts: the Get Cash modal is a placeholder and no client script calls a Marketplace prompt. Roblox's purchase dialog cannot be styled. Decide what the restyled cash store shows until products exist, and what the cash chip's plus button does.

Start and loading screens: the sheet leaves the logo art unchanged, but the status text reads LOADING NEO TOKYO and the artwork is NeoTokyoStreet01 while the title is Pulse Racers. Decide the string, and whether the Play and Shop buttons and the progress bar restyle.

Dealership wayfinding signs: six SurfaceGui labels (BUY, CUSTOMIZE, CUSTOMIZATION, DEALERSHIP, ENTRANCE) use Gotham and American spelling beside a UI that says CUSTOMISE. They are Workspace art; decide whether they follow the new typeface and spelling.

World guidance colours: next-gate pill (mint), finish gate (yellow), wrong-way warning, route arrows, activity beacons, start-zone aura and the gold onboarding trail use colours outside the five roles. Decide a token mapping or declare them world art.
Other CoreGui: emotes menu (UserEmotesEnabled true), empty backpack, self view, captures and the Esc menu stay Roblox-styled. Decide which CoreGui types are switched off for the game as a whole.

Roblox accessibility settings: no script handles the player's Text Size setting (PreferredTextSize) or reduced motion. Fixed dense panels will grow or clip at Largest. Decide whether labels are capped or tested at that setting.

Baked-colour art: map icons (cyan, pink, blue), teal mobile pedal and arrow images, blue boost icon, grey lock, the outline racing icon atlas and the medal atlas cannot be tinted to the new roles. Each needs a keep, redraw or replace decision.
Core notifications: Roblox toasts (badges, friend requests, and the Studio test-cash message sent through SetCore) keep the engine look and appear bottom-right, where the sheet puts the speed gauge.
contradictions: Switch model. Racing-menus, garage-core, map, racing-session and foundation-startup say leave old scripts byte-identical and pick new modules in ClientBase. The sheet (step 2), freeroam-desktop (ActivityClient) and mobile-onboarding (3.12 B) rely on RacingUIComponents becoming style-aware in place. Both cannot hold: the backup draws through that module.

Untouched backup. Each reader says its old scripts stay untouched, but the union needs edits to ClientBase, LoadingTransitionRuntime, InitialLoadingAndStartScreenClient, SharedTopNotificationUI, GarageEntranceClient, OwnedGarageClient, RouteGuide, MapIconLayer and probably OnboardingClient. The plan needs one explicit list of edited old scripts.

Owned-garage desk. Garage-owned-entry says the management desk needs no work because it follows the shared garage view. Garage-core's recommended option B leaves GarageWorkspaceUI untouched in its old canvas, which the desk still uses. Under option B the desk stays old-style unless it gets its own new module.

Flag timing. Foundation-startup says the style attribute on Config.UI is present at ReplicatedFirst time with no extra wait. Garage-owned-entry says a server-set attribute may not have arrived and the first loading screen needs a fallback. Both agree a fresh server's first joiner can get the default.

In-race map. Map notes say no in-race minimap exists. Racing-session notes, and RaceSessionPresentationClient lines 31-69, show a desktop route-map panel fed by Config.Racing.HudMapCatalog. The sheet's 'minimap as in free roam' replaces that panel; it does not fill an empty space.

Michroma config values. The sheet says four, foundation-startup three, fonts-assets five. Studio has five: Theme.FontFamily, Racing.Typography.FontFamily, GarageExperience.FontFamily, and DesktopFreeRoamHud.Typography.PrimaryFont and BodyFont (the last two hold the name, not a family path).

Colour folders. The sheet says three near-identical folders. Only DesktopFreeRoamHud.Colours and Racing.Colours match (HUD adds HighSpeed). GarageExperience has different values and one reader, GarageEntranceClient. Theme is a different legacy palette that also holds cash-count behaviour. The literal count is 273 in 37 client scripts, not about 230.

ZIndexBehavior. Garage-owned-entry and roblox-platform say two ScreenGuis use Global. Source: two set it explicitly (shared confirmation, in-race HUD) and nine more never set it, so default to Global: race browser, entry, countdown, queue, route guide, results, transition, owned-garage browser, entrance status.
Mobile minimap size. Map notes give MinimapSize 180; mobile-onboarding gives 170. The live attribute on Config.UI.MobileFreeRoamHud is 170.

Typeface. The sheet and roblox-platform assume Titillium Web, whose fixed-width digits need no digit cells. Fonts-assets ranks Barlow first (proportional digits) and shows the sheet's sizes are CSS sizes: Titillium needs 1.57 times, putting ScreenTitle at 125, above the TextSize cap of 100.

Glow. The sheet and fonts-assets plan uploaded 9-slice glow images (SliceCenter is used nowhere today). Roblox-platform says UIShadow, reported fully released in June 2026, replaces them with no uploads. Neither was rendered; the choice changes the asset list and the instance budget.

Delivery tool. The sheet names scripts/studio_delivery.py for every step. Docs-and-delivery shows its capture guard rejects v3 (studio_capture.py line 11 lists three other place ids, confirmed), and that new ModuleScripts and typed config need a migration route not yet proven in v3.

Lane. The sheet's contract says Standard. Docs-and-delivery says the token, component and switch step is High-Risk: new modules, a start-up selection in ClientBase and a new server-to-client flag projection.

Acceptance test. The sheet requires rerender counts unchanged and instance counts within 10% of today. Readers recommend pooled rows, lazy modals and no full rebuilds, which deliberately change both (the desktop HUD builds about 610 instances, 420 of them hidden modals).

Phone layout. The sheet says phones use the same clusters, with the minimap bottom-left. Map and mobile notes show the phone minimap is top-right because steering controls hold the bottom-left, and racing and garage menus are the desktop canvas shrunk to about 0.43.

Results XP. The sheet says all results figures come from the server result payload, including driver XP. Racing-session shows neither RaceFinished nor TimeTrialFinished carries XP; it arrives later as player attributes.

Key hints. The sheet allows one key cap, on the world Start banner. The full map's hint strip is all key legends and the Controls modal is rows of key caps; map notes say the map controls are undiscoverable without them.

Names in the sheet. Core.FeatureFlags is in ServerStorage and unreadable by clients; GarageReplacementComponents does not exist (the card is GarageComponents.VehicleCard). Every reader agrees, so the sheet's contract lines for the switch and the shared card are wrong as written.

RaceTransitionClient. Racing-session says keep it unchanged under both styles. It draws a label with a Michroma literal, so the new style would still show the old typeface during race transitions unless that is accepted or the label is tokenised.
openQuestions: Which switch model is approved: new modules selected in ClientBase, style-aware shared components edited in place, or a stated mix per screen? Which old scripts may be edited, and is the backup frozen or kept in step with behaviour fixes?

How does the client learn the style before ReplicatedFirst loading and ClientBase run: a server-written attribute from FeatureFlags (a new server owner) or a plain replicated config value? What does a fresh server's first joiner get, and is a per-player preview override wanted?

Does the build include the navigation changes (hub removal, Owned/Buy merge)? They remove the three cards onboarding highlights on the saved page id CustomisationHome and need new controller logic, not only new views.

Onboarding finds targets by instance name, button text and attributes across every screen, and locks any button named Car, Race or Garage. Will new views keep those names and texts, or is OnboardingClient changed in the same delivery?

Final typeface: it needs one live capture of Barlow, Roboto Condensed and Titillium Web on a dense screen at three resolutions. How are numbers above TextSize 100 drawn (UIScale or digit sprites), and are sizes specified as cap heights?

Not yet rendered: hairline sharpness under fractional UIScale, UIShadow glow against 9-slice, text above 100 px under UIScale, and a CanvasGroup round minimap on a low-end phone. Each needs a throwaway Play capture before the components are fixed.

One shared scale and safe-area source: what maximum scale above 1080p, what phone floor, and do garage, race menus and results get a real phone layout rather than a shrunk desktop canvas? The 11 px and 48 px rules cannot be met by scaling alone.

CoreGui policy: is the Roblox player list disabled, where does chat sit, are health and emotes hidden, and is a custom gamepad selection image set? These decide where the top-left and top-right clusters can go.

Is a custom proximity-prompt renderer in scope? It needs Style Custom on server-created prompts (TimeTrialServer, VehicleAccessServer, OwnedGarageManagement), on garage templates and on two Workspace prompts, plus one client renderer.

Colour exceptions still undecided: tutorial gold beside cash yellow, tier colours, the yellow finish gate, pink activity routes, baked-colour map icons, affordability green and red, and the three Activity theme colours passed as meaning.
Results: does driver XP come from a new server payload field or from the client watching XpIntoRank and Rank? Do medals, leaderboard, lap list and finishing order stay, since the mockup omits them?
In-race map: restyle the existing desktop route-image panel, or add a live round minimap with new per-frame cost? Phones have neither today.

What UI audio contract do new components follow? PresentationAudioClient plays hover and click on every GuiButton with visible content; tile rails, backdrops and tabs need rules for UIAudioSilent, UIAudioSuppressClick and custom cues.

Delivery route in v3: is the capture place guard extended (TOOL-05), or is one new installer built that creates ModuleScripts and Color3Value config? Do new config values survive save and reopen, given Theme values were dropped once?

Hybrid devices (touch plus keyboard or mouse) start both HUDs today, and four different mobile tests exist. What single form-factor rule do the new modules use, and does it re-evaluate when input changes?

ScreenGui naming: RaceLifecyclePresentationClient destroys any ScreenGui named RaceHud, RaceEntry and nine others; two scripts look up DriveHUD; FullMapUI and onboarding need DesktopFreeRoamHud and Minimap. Is there one registry of reserved and required names for new views?

Copy ownership: server replies supply toast and status text in sentence case, strings such as LOADING NEO TOKYO are literals, and Config.UI.Racing.Copy holds some. Does the restyle normalise case and wording, and where do strings live?
Settings rows that do nothing (UI scale, graphics, speed unit, sliders, Reset Defaults): restyle as they are, hide, or implement? A working UI scale setting would multiply the new shared scale.
